issue.title: Improve CCS network faults detection

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
When using Cross Cluster Search and a remote cluster becomes unreachable due to network issues, it takes the CCS node a while to detect that. This seems particularly bad if a firewall in-between drops connections, as it makes CCS searches hang, despite TCP connections can be initiated from the CCS node to the remote cluster nodes on port 9300.

This has been reported on our [forum](https://discuss.elastic.co/t/elasticsearch-ccs-client-get-timeout-when-remote-cluster-is-isolated-by-firewall/152019) and also on #30247 .

The following are changes that we could make to improve this:

- [x] allow to enable scheduled pings directed to remote clusters without affecting intra-cluster communication (see also #10189) (#34753)
- [x] possibly adapt the transport ping to come back with a response (#35441)
- [x] add support for a timeout to the transport ping? (users should do this at the TCP level and #59222 documents how)
- [ ] consider enabling transport pings by default for remote clusters with a sensible default interval (see also #5067, some discussion happened in #34753)
- [ ] given that CCS searches are timing out in the initial search_shards phase, we also may want to apply a sensible timeout and/or make the timeout configurable (see #32678)

issue.title: Fail fast remote cluster requests

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
When using the skip_unavailable option on remote clusters, searches and similar actions should fail quickly instead of waiting on connections to be reestablished.

This PR makes it so that search, field caps, resolve index, and term enum cross-cluster requests fail fast when skip_unavailable is set to true on the given cluster. Internal cross-cluster requests (e.g. license checks, CCR, etc.) still continue waiting on connection attempts.

Closes #74773

issue.title: [Monitoring] Handle failed/unavailable CCS requests

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Fixes for quality problems that affect the customer experience

repository.name: kibana
repository.description: Your window into all of your data

issue.body:
The queries which are used when accessing SM API are prepended with `*:` (on all `.monitoring-*` indices) when calling ES's `_search` API. This is to also access remote clusters` data, and is on by default. As a result when one of the remote clusters is not responding the UI stops working.

Possible workaround:
```yml
# 6.1 - 7.6
xpack.monitoring.ccs.enabled: false

# 7.7+
monitoring.ui.ccs.enabled: false
```

Looking at the code we do indeed use `ignoreUnavailable: true` which translates to `skip_unavailable: true` in ES, so I'm assuming this to be a bug rather than an enhancement. Since, the API call should still pass gracefully, and the UI should still work without any interruptions/blockers

Related: https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/57596
Related: https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/36323
Related: https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/82143

issue.title: Integrate CCS with new search_shards API

labels.name: :Search/Search
labels.description: Search-related issues that do not fall into other categories

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
This PR integrates CCS with the new search_shards API. With this change, we will be able to skip shards on the coordinator on remote clusters using the timestamps stored in the cluster state.

Relates #94534
Closes #93730
